title: Next.js schedules a security update as Anthropic opens AI scans to open source
summary: An October 8 Next.js notice sets an October 14 date for three upstream security fixes. On the same day, Anthropic introduced a free, opt-in vulnerability scanner for eligible open-source maintainers.
imageAlt: Line illustration of a browser security notice beside a scanning lens inspecting an open-source package
imageCaption: Original illustration of a pending framework security update and an independent AI scanning service; not a product screenshot.

sections.heading: Next.js gives teams advance notice of an October 14 patch
paragraphs: The Next.js team said on October 8 that it plans an out-of-band security update for Wednesday, October 14, 2026. The planned release addresses three vulnerabilities in upstream dependencies: two rated Critical and one High. The team said two of the fixes were postponed from its September security release while it coordinated with upstream projects.

This is a notice, not the patch itself. Next.js says the full advisories will accompany the update, including impact, affected versions, and upgrade instructions. Those details are not in the October 8 notice, so it would be premature to claim that a particular version is vulnerable or already fixed.

sections.heading: Preparation can start before the affected versions are known
paragraphs: Teams running Next.js can identify which applications they operate and who will review the October 14 advisories. That is a practical preparation step, not a substitute for the official version-specific guidance. Once patched versions are released, the Next.js team recommends upgrading as soon as the update is available.

The announcement does not say that upgrading to the already released Next.js 16.4 resolves these upcoming vulnerabilities. A dependency inventory and a planned testing window are more useful now than guessing at a package version or treating an unreleased fix as installed.

sections.heading: Anthropic offers maintainers a faster stream of findings
paragraphs: Also on October 8, Anthropic launched OSS Scanner as part of its Cyber Mission. Eligible open-source projects can opt in to periodic scans by Anthropic's models at no cost. The service sends maintainers reports with an explanation, a proof of concept, and a suggested fix when one is available. Anthropic says enrollment is intended for core maintainers of established projects with the capacity to investigate incoming reports.

The faster path comes with an important limit: these reports are generated by models and sent without human review. Anthropic explicitly warns that some details, including severity ratings, may be inaccurate. Its expectation of a true-positive rate above 90% is a vendor projection, not an independently verified result or a guarantee for any project's reports.

sections.heading: Scanning adds evidence, not an automatic repair
paragraphs: Anthropic's service is separate from the Next.js security announcement; there is no claim that it found or will fix the three upstream issues. For maintainers who enroll, reports still need reproduction, severity review, and a controlled patch process. Anthropic's scanner documentation says an initial scan is followed by recurring scans, while the frequency may vary with demand.

The two announcements illustrate different parts of the same software-security workflow: a framework team coordinating and publishing a patch, and an AI tool surfacing possible defects for maintainers to assess. Neither removes the need to verify findings and test a fix before deployment.

sources.label: Anthropic Frontier Red Team · OSS Scanner documentation · accessed October 9, 2026

zh-TW.title: Next.js 預告安全更新，Anthropic 開放 AI 掃描開源專案
zh-TW.summary: Next.js 在 10 月 8 日預告將於 14 日修補三項上游依賴漏洞；同一天，Anthropic 推出讓符合資格的開源維護者自願申請、免費使用的漏洞掃描服務。
zh-TW.imageAlt: 瀏覽器安全公告旁，一個掃描鏡頭正在檢視開源軟體套件的線條插畫
zh-TW.imageCaption: 本站原創插畫，呈現尚待發布的框架安全更新與獨立的 AI 掃描服務，非產品截圖。

sections.heading: Next.js 提前預告 10 月 14 日的修補
paragraphs: Next.js 團隊在 10 月 8 日表示，計畫於 2026 年 10 月 14 日（週三）發布例行時程之外的安全更新。預定修補的項目是上游依賴套件中的三項漏洞，其中兩項評為 Critical、一項評為 High。團隊說，有兩項修補因需要與上游專案協調，從 9 月的安全版本延至這次預定的更新。
這是一則預告，並不是修補程式本身。Next.js 表示，完整公告會隨更新發布，屆時才會提供影響範圍、受影響版本與升級方式。10 月 8 日的文章尚未列出這些細節，因此不能據此斷定某個版本已受影響，或已完成修補。

sections.heading: 在版本資訊公布前，仍可先整理升級準備
paragraphs: 使用 Next.js 的團隊現在可以盤點正在運作的應用程式，並指定誰負責閱讀 10 月 14 日的安全公告。這是事前準備，不能取代屆時官方針對版本的指引。待修補版本發布後，Next.js 團隊建議盡快升級。
預告並未表示已發布的 Next.js 16.4 能解決這幾項待修補漏洞。此時比起猜測套件版本，整理依賴清單並預留測試時間，才能在正式公告出來後依實際影響範圍採取行動。

sections.heading: Anthropic 讓維護者更快收到潛在漏洞報告
paragraphs: 同樣在 10 月 8 日，Anthropic 在 Cyber Mission 計畫下推出 OSS Scanner。符合資格的開源專案可以自願加入，免費接受 Anthropic 模型的定期掃描。報告會提供問題說明、概念驗證，以及在有可行方案時提供修補建議。Anthropic 表示，這項服務主要面向有能力處理報告的成熟專案核心維護者。
較快取得結果也有明確限制：這些報告由模型產生，寄送前不經人工審查。Anthropic 提醒，內容可能不準確，嚴重程度的判定也可能有誤。其預期真陽性率可超過 90%，是廠商的預估，並非獨立驗證的結果，更不是對個別專案的保證。

sections.heading: 掃描提供線索，不會自動完成修補
paragraphs: Anthropic 的服務與 Next.js 的安全預告彼此獨立；沒有資料顯示它發現或將修復上述三項上游漏洞。加入掃描服務的維護者仍需重現問題、檢查嚴重程度，並以受控流程製作與測試修補。OSS Scanner 文件指出，首次掃描後會持續定期掃描，但頻率可能隨使用量變動。
這兩項公告呈現軟體安全流程中的不同環節：框架團隊協調並發布修補，AI 工具則提出待維護者查核的潛在問題。無論是哪一種情況，上線前仍需要確認問題與驗證修補結果。
